etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English difficultee, from Old French difficulté, from Latin difficultas, from difficul, older form of difficilis (“hard to do, difficult”), from dis- + facilis (“easy”); see difficile and difficult. Equivalent to dis- +‎ facile +‎ -ty. Also analysable as difficult +‎ -y, though the adjective is historically a backformation from the noun.

definitions.definition: The state of being difficult, or hard to do.
An obstacle that hinders achievement of a goal.

quote.citation: 1860, Photographic news for amateur photographers, volumes 3-4, page 113:
quote.text: The difficulties of photoheliography consist principally in the rapidity with which the sun's image acts upon the sensitive film.

quote.citation: 2019 June 27, Lauren Gambino, “Democratic 2020 candidates clash on healthcare, immigration and economy in first debate”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: The two-hour debate was briefly stalled by a technical difficulty with the moderators’ microphones.

definitions.definition: (sometimes in the plural) Physical danger from the environment, especially with risk of drowning

quote.citation: 2016 February 24, Catherine Shanahan, “Boy, 13, drowns after getting into difficulty in river”, in Irish Examiner:
quote.text: The three teenagers, a girl and two boys, were playing by the river when it is believed they got into difficulty.

quote.citation: 2016 March 14, “Kayaker rescued after getting into difficulty”, in Bournemouth Echo‎[2]:
quote.text: Members of the public had called 999 as they were concerned the kayaker was in difficulty around the headland race due to very strong spring tides and choppy seas with the kayaker making no headway.

quote.citation: 2016 March 19, Neil Shaw, “Teens rescued from Dartmoor after getting into difficulty”, in Plymouth Herald:
quote.text: A group of young people had to be rescued from Dartmoor on Friday night after getting into difficulty during a Duke of Edinburgh exercise.  […]  A 16-year-old girl required medical attention and a medic was winched down to the site by helicopter.

definitions.definition: That which cannot be easily understood or believed.
